solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Four employ five climbing US volcano

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the run of pieces is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals
to employ is to use
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An American's description of a volcano with figures attached to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns the whole run IV + USE + V, giving VESUVI; US is then added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesuvius is the famous volcano near Naples, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Cash in one's chips having secured 100 in gamble

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second fast inside it, as if it had secured it

parts.note: slang for to die
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes a hundred on a roll before quitting the casino.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cash in one's chips' looks like casino talk but is an idiom for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: To dice is to gamble, playing games of chance with dice.

clue.text: Trainee ultimately failing to pass

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word trainee

parts.note: a lapse is a failing or slip

explanation.surface: A trainee is going to flunk the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' looks like an exam result, but it means time going by.
explanation.definitionFit: When time passes it is said to elapse; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: A fool may show bitterness about the City after one month

indicators.note: the bitterness piece is placed after the month and the one

parts.note: I is one in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the word for bitterness goes round the City abbreviation

parts.note: bile means bitterness or ill temper
EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone turning sour on the City a month into the job shows he is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the City inside the bitterness word, and 'after' puts that whole piece behind one and month; EC is the City of London's postcode area.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbecile is a stupid person, a synonym of fool.

clue.text: Thirsty, swallow one drink

parts.note: dry can mean thirsty
the martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Feeling thirsty, someone downs a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' reads as a verb but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry martini is a gin and vermouth cocktail, so an example of a drink.

clue.text: Poll everyone in base, except Tom?

indicators.note: the word for everyone sits inside the remains of the base word
except says the name Tom is removed from the base word

parts.note: bottom means base
taken as written and removed
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A survey of everybody at a military base, apart from one man called Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military camp but is the bottom; 'except' strips the name, and 'in' puts everyone inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot is a vote, a synonym of poll as in an election.

clue.text: Athenian statesman replies unexpectedly about leader of country

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the single letter
unexpectedly signals the letters of replies come out in a surprising new order
leader of means the first letter of country

explanation.surface: A Greek politician gives a surprising answer on national leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' turns REPLIES into PERILES, and 'about' puts C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pericles was the leading statesman of Athens in its fifth-century golden age.

clue.text: One who drinks with a meal?

definitions.meaning: someone who sups or sips a drink

explanation.definitionFit: Read as sup plus -er it is a drinker; as an ordinary word it is the evening meal.

clue.text: Cannon right next to second sailor

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second
tar is a traditional word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A gun placed to the right of the sailor who is second in line.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortar is a short artillery piece, a type of cannon.

clue.text: Phoney English dandy

parts.note: a dud is a fake or something that fails

explanation.surface: A fake English gentleman of fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Dude originally meant a fastidious dandy, a synonym.

clue.text: What a waiter may use in shower works

parts.note: to pepper is to shower with small things
a mill is a works or factory

explanation.surface: A waiter's tool in a factory's washroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shower' is the verb to pepper, not a washroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiters offer a grinder of black pepper at table, so it is an item a waiter uses.

clue.text: Plagiarist could make head of publishing very angry

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of publishing

parts.note: irate means very angry

explanation.surface: A copier of others' work would enrage a publishing boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of publishing' looks like a job title but just gives P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate in publishing is someone who copies others' work without permission, a plagiarist.

clue.text: PA a fellow uses in resort

parts.note: man is a fellow

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means arrange these letters again

explanation.surface: A personal assistant whom a man takes on at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot but means re-sort: USES IN becomes UENSIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis takes dictation or copies manuscripts, the job of a personal assistant.

clue.text: Leave the country, Arabian state, around middle of night

indicators.note: the state's name goes around the single letter

parts.note: an emirate, such as one of the United Arab Emirates

indicators.note: middle of points to the central letter of night

explanation.surface: Fleeing abroad from a Gulf state in the dead of night.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to settle elsewhere.

clue.text: Drink with beer in, readily available after end of matches

indicators.note: after places the word for readily available behind that letter
end of points to the last letter of matches

parts.note: handy means close at hand

explanation.surface: Beer is easy to get hold of when the matches are over.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a drink of beer mixed with lemonade, so beer is in it.

clue.text: Envoy bringing certificate on time

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate of qualification

explanation.surface: An ambassador arriving with a qualification just in time.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is an official representing a country abroad, an envoy.

clue.text: Large body of soldiers, say, outflanked by hero

indicators.note: outflanked means surrounded on both sides, so the hero word wraps the other

parts.note: a lion is a brave person, a hero
eg, for example, is what say signals

explanation.surface: An army unit, for instance, outmanoeuvred by a brave man.
explanation.definitionFit: A legion was a Roman army division, a large body of soldiers.

clue.text: Leap in the dark after small number? Not likely!

indicators.note: the leap word follows the number abbreviation

parts.note: No is the abbreviation for number
a chance is a gamble, a leap in the dark

explanation.surface: Taking a risk on a low number? Hardly likely to pay off!
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation meaning something will not happen, the same as not likely.

clue.text: Girl to instruct in Salvation Army

indicators.note: the instruct word goes inside the Salvation Army abbreviation

parts.note: to tell is to instruct or order

explanation.surface: A young woman giving orders within the Salvation Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a girl's name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Prostitute in street, peculiar blue-eyed girl?

parts.note: rum means odd or peculiar
a blue-eyed boy or girl is a favourite, a pet

explanation.surface: A streetwalker who is an oddly favoured young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue-eyed' is the British idiom for a favourite, not eye colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumpet is an old-fashioned word for a prostitute.

clue.text: Capo to kill boxer, perhaps

parts.note: to top someone is slang for killing them
a boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss orders the death of a prizefighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' looks like a fighter; it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A capo is a Mafia boss, the leader of the pack.

clue.text: Piece of cake catching large seal

indicators.note: the easy-task word catches the size letter inside it

parts.note: a cinch is something very easy

explanation.surface: A slice of cake grabbed by a big marine mammal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seal' is the verb to settle a deal, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To clinch a deal is to seal it, settling it finally.

clue.text: Is concerned about son getting pet

parts.note: cares about means is concerned about

explanation.surface: Worrying about a son who wants an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like an animal but is the verb to fondle.
explanation.definitionFit: To caress is to stroke lovingly, a synonym of the verb pet.

clue.text: Cricketer LBW, person I bamboozled

indicators.note: bamboozled means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A batsman given out leg before wicket complains he was fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: LBW, leg before wicket, is a way of being out in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin bowler is a cricketer who turns the ball, an example of a cricketer.

clue.text: Ambush a two-wheeled carriage

definitions.meaning: a snare laid to catch someone
a light horse-drawn cart on two wheels

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a snare and a light horse-drawn gig.

clue.text: Rent in Le Touquet, or Nice?

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside these words

explanation.surface: Paying for lodgings in one French resort or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like a payment but is the past participle of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent as the past participle of rend means ripped, a synonym.

clue.text: Italian embraced by girl in film

indicators.note: the girl's name wraps around the Italian abbreviation

parts.note: Lola is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An Italian man in a girl's arms in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita is a film by Stanley Kubrick, from Nabokov's novel.

clue.text: A bishop's pamphlet, hard to understand

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, with the S of the possessive
a tract is a religious pamphlet

explanation.surface: A clergyman's leaflet is difficult to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstract ideas are theoretical and hard to grasp, a synonym.
